facts.statement: The type specimen of Kaatedocus consists of a well-preserved skull and cervical vertebrae found in the lower Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: It is known from well-preserved skull and cervical vertebrae which were collected in the lower part of the Morrison Formation.

facts.statement: A specimen previously thought to be Barosaurus was reinterpreted as Kaatedocus in 2015 based on phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: In 2015, based on specimen-level phylogenetic analysis, one of these specimens (AMNH FARB 7530) was reinterpreted to belong to Kaatedocus.

facts.statement: In 1989, a team led by Hans-Jakob Siber found 450 additional bones near the original quarry site, which are now held by the Swiss Aathal Dinosaur Museum.
facts.quote: In 1989 the site was reopened by Hans-Jakob Siber, the founder of the Swiss Aathal Dinosaur Museum. His team immediately adjacent to the old Howe Quarry discovered another 450 bones that became part of the collection of the Swiss museum.

facts.statement: Kaatedocus siberi was named in 2012 by Emanuel Tschopp and Octávio Mateus.
facts.quote: In 2012 this was named Kaatedocus siberi, by the Swiss palaeontologist Emanuel Tschopp, who as a boy had visited the excavations, and his Portuguese colleague Octávio Mateus.

facts.statement: Kaatedocus lived during the Middle Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian stage) in what is now northern Wyoming, United States.
facts.quote: Kaatedocus is a genus of flagellicaudatan sauropod known from the middle Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian stage) of northern Wyoming, United States.

facts.statement: The type individual of Kaatedocus was estimated to be approximately 14 meters long, making it relatively small compared to most diplodocids.
facts.quote: Kaatedocus was relatively small compared to most diplodocids. The type individual was estimated to have been approximately 14 m long.

facts.statement: The neck of Kaatedocus was composed of at least 14 vertebrae, a number comparable to typical diplodocids.
facts.quote: The neck was composed of at least 14 vertebrae, comparable to the typical number in diplodocids.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Kaatedocus represents an animal estimated to be 12 to 14 meters long, indicating a body weight of 14 tonnes.
facts.quote: El espécimen tipo representa un animal con una longitud estimada de 12 a 14 metros, lo que indica un peso corporal de 14 toneladas.

facts.statement: Tschopp suggests that larger adult specimens of Kaatedocus could have reached a length of 16 to 18 meters.
facts.quote: Tschopp cree que los especímenes adultos más grandes podían alcanzar una longitud de unos 16 a 18 metros.

facts.statement: The skull of Kaatedocus is flattened and wide, with narrow teeth at the front, as deduced from tooth cavities since the teeth themselves are lost.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Kaatedocus es aplanado y ancho, con dientes estrechos hacia adelante, hasta donde se puede deducir de las cavidades de los dientes porque los dientes se han perdido.

facts.statement: The tail vertebrae of Kaatedocus have a single keel.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la cola tienen una sola quilla.

facts.statement: Whitlock and Wilson (2020) argue that Kaatedocus is the most basal dicraeosaurid, a position they consider more likely than being a diplodocid.
facts.quote: On the other hand, Whitlock and Wilson (2020) find Kaatedocus to be the most basal dicraeosaurid, finding such a position more likely than being a diplodocid.

facts.statement: Kaatedocus is classified within the family Diplodocidae.
facts.quote: familia: Diplodocidae

facts.statement: Kaatedocus belongs to the subfamily Diplodocinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Diplodocinae

facts.statement: It is debated whether certain skull features of Kaatedocus are specific to Diplodocidae or general traits of Flagellicaudata, as it is unknown if dicraeosaurids possessed these features.
facts.quote: They found the first character to be a more general character diagnostic of Flagellicaudata, because it is currently unknown if dicraeosaurids possessed this feature.

facts.statement: Kaatedocus fossils were found in northern Wyoming, USA.
facts.quote: Sus restos se encontraron en el norte de Wyoming, Estados Unidos.

facts.statement: The species is known from a well-preserved skull and a series of cervical vertebrae collected from the Morrison Formation.
facts.quote: Es conocido a partir de un cráneo y una serie de vértebras cervicales bien preservadas que fueron recolectadas en la Formación Morrison.

facts.statement: The only known species, Kaatedocus siberi, was described in 2012 by Emanuel Tschopp and Octávio Mateus.
facts.quote: La única especie conocida, es el tipo Kaatedocus siberi, descrito en 2012 por Emanuel Tschopp y Octávio Mateus.

facts.statement: Only 10% of the originally discovered fossils survived, including a skull.
facts.quote: Solo un 10% de los fósiles sobrevivieron, entre estos un cráneo.

facts.statement: The site was reopened in 1989 by Hans-Jakob Siber, founder of the Sauriermuseum Aathal in Switzerland.
facts.quote: En 1989 el sitio fue vuelto a abrir por Hans-Jakob Siber, el fundador del Sauriermuseum Aathal en Suiza.

facts.statement: Siber's team discovered an additional 450 bones at the adjacent Cantera Quarry, which joined the Swiss museum collection.
facts.quote: Su equipo empezó a trabajar en la adyacente Cantera Quarry y descubrió otros 450 huesos que se volvieron parte de la colección del museo suizo.

facts.statement: The genus was named Kaatedocus siberi in 2012 by Swiss paleontologist Emanuel Tschopp and his Portuguese colleague Octávio Mateus.
facts.quote: En 2012 esta fue denominada Kaatedocus siberi, por el paleontólogo suizo Emanuel Tschopp, quien visitó de joven las excavaciones, y su colega portugués Octávio Mateus.

facts.statement: The genus name combines a reference to its relative Diplodocus with the diminutive suffix ~kaate from the Crow language.
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina una referencia a su pariente Diplodocus con el sufijo diminutivo en idioma crow ~kaate.

facts.statement: The species name honors Hans-Jakob Siber.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie es en homenaje de Siber.

facts.statement: In 2017, Tschopp and Mateus positioned Kaatedocus as the most basal diplodocine during a phylogenetic review associated with the description of the genus Galeamopus.
facts.quote: Después de colocar en el grupo de la hermana de Barosaurus en su vasta síntesis Diplodocidae en 2015, Emanuel Tschopp y Octavio Mateus lo posicionan como el más basal de diplodócinos en ocasión de una revisión filogenética durante la descripción de la nueva Género Galeamopus en 2017.

facts.statement: Kaatedocus belongs to the parent group Dicraeosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Dicraeosauridae

facts.statement: Kaatedocus is classified in the family Dicraeosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Dicraeosauridae

facts.statement: Kaatedocus is a member of the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Kaatedocus lived during the Kimmeridgian stage, between 154.8 and 149.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Kimmeridgian to Kimmeridgian (154.8 to 149.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Research by Andreas Christian and Armin Schmitt suggests that Kaatedocus held its neck in a vertical position, confirmed by studies of its vestibular system.
facts.quote: En 2010 Andreas Christian usó las vértebras bien preservadas para apoyar su hipótesis de que los cuellos de los saurópodos se mantenían en una posición más bien vertical, lo cual fue confirmado por Armin Schmitt al estudiar el sistema vestibular de Kaatedocus.
